units.text: INT. FARMHOUSE KITCHEN - EARLY MORNING
A low-beamed room that smells of woodsmoke and yeast.
A cast-iron stove ticks.
Copper pans hang from a rack above a scrubbed pine table.
Through the window, frost coats a vegetable garden and a rooster stands on the fence post like a weathervane.
NANA PHILOMENA (80s, shawl over a flannel nightgown, hands knotted as old rope) kneads dough at the table, her movements slow and exact.
Across from her, her grandson TEODOR (7, pajamas with rocket ships, hair in a cowlick) kneels on a chair, a ball of dough in each fist.
Mine's a rabbit.
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: It looks like a potato.
units.name: NANA PHILOMENA

units.text: It's a rabbit potato.
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: She smiles, dusts flour from her thumb, and takes his dough.
Pinches two ears from the top.
Hands it back.
Now it's a rabbit.
units.name: NANA PHILOMENA

units.text: He sets it on the tray beside the others.
A row of small misshapen animals.
Outside, the rooster crows once, late.
Nana?
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: Mm.
units.name: NANA PHILOMENA

units.text: Will you teach me the bread song?
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: There's no song.
units.name: NANA PHILOMENA

units.text: Mum says there is.
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: Your mother talks too much.
units.name: NANA PHILOMENA

units.text: She begins to hum, a low, wavering tune, kneading in time.
He hums with her, a half-step off, and neither corrects the other.
